items.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03
items.q: He played, he played as near as Connie as anybody ever heard in my life. Yes. Well, I've read.

ctx.x: Connie and Bigard and Hodges and those people.

He played, he played as near as Connie as anybody ever heard in my life. Yes. Well, I've read. And he can listen to the album that we had, the rockin' and swing and the sheikin' and she, the same tonation that's the same. The same tonation, the same figures. That's rated up right there with Connie.

I don't know if you've ever seen it. I couldn't make a copy of that. It's a solo. Jazz on record, 1970s and 1970s. They had a bunch of different ones. Anyway, I ask you why you joined the band. What made for a good big band? What, the big band? Yeah. Oh, the sound made it good to me. I love the sound. I love the sound. The sound made it good to me. I love the sound. The sound made it good to me.
